Now compare the two runs with acycle_compare for a side-by-side of saved parameters without recompute.

Peaks nearly identical for the high-frequency cluster and 57 m; only the low-frequency pair shifted: 270.33→263.22, 238.15→232.61 (frequency 0.00370→0.00380, 0.00420→0.00430). Powers slightly changed (0.663→0.673, 0.630→0.646). Robust AR(1) rho 0.4336→0.4333.

So the difference: primarily the long-period end (232–263 m) moves by ~2.5% and gains a bit of power; everything from ~65 m down to 13 m is essentially unchanged (peak powers identical to 4-5 digits for most).

Let me get compare output and view the new figures to describe differences (e.g., the 500 m stripe).

content.text:
The two evolution images look essentially identical (window 699.86 m fixed, EvoFFT operates on detrended windows with its own internal handling — actually the EvoFFT likely re-detrends per window; anyway nearly identical). The stripe at ~500 m is still there in both.

Differences in the full-record spectrum: only the low-frequency pair shifted 270→263, 238→233 m, with slightly higher power; and the robust AR(1) rho barely changed.

Also note in the new spectrum figure: power at very low frequency (f<0.01) appears... the baseline showed a peak near f~0.005 rising toward 10^0 at the leftmost. In the new one, the large peak is still at ~0.017. Hard to compare visually in detail beyond peaks table.

Important: why almost no change? Because the peak at 57 m sits well inside the >500 m bandpass; stronger detrending (shorter 500 m span) removes more power at long wavelengths, so periods near 200–300 m shift and their power changes most, while periods <~65 m are essentially untouched.

Note: span 0.25 → 500 m window; LOWESS removes structure longer than ~500 m; so 263/233 m peaks are on the edge of the filter's passband — exactly where the change is.

Also record: evolution window remained 699.86 m (explicit parameter, not derived from span) — so evolution figures essentially identical; the limited change demonstrates the EvoFFT is insensitive to this detrend choice (or that evolution uses per-window detrending). State factually: evolution window unchanged at 699.86 m, and the two evolution plots are near-identical, which is expected because the low-frequency band affected by span is at the very bottom of the evolution panel.

I should quantify differences in the answer: 57.16 m unchanged exactly (same frequency bin), power 1.3850 → 1.3855 (+0.03%); 65.37 m 0.5308 → 0.5299; 17.6 m 0.5168→0.5167; 13.21 0.46518→0.46518; 17.34 0.44903→0.44905; 14.11 0.44165→0.44167. Low freq: 270.33→263.22 m (−2.6%), power 0.663→0.673 (+1.5%); 238.15→232.61 (−2.3%), 0.6305→0.6457 (+2.4%). rho 0.43362→0.43334.

Present figures. Then conclusions: main periodicity robust to detrend span; low-frequency peaks not robust (position moves ~2-3% and they're near passband edge) → shouldn't be cited as fixed values.
